set_d.instruction: Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below.
set_d.passage:
Reaffirming the importance of reformed multilateralism in a world riven with unilateral actions by superpowers emerged as a binding theme of the 18th BRICS Summit and the New Delhi Declaration. The Summit’s success could be measured by three main parameters — the participation of members at the highest levels, the importance given to intra-BRICS trade cooperation mechanisms and the consensus achieved by Indian negotiators in forging a joint statement in a time of war. The government should be commended for ensuring that Iran and the UAE, two rivals in the West Asian conflict, used the occasion for their highest-level bilateral meeting since the war began.
The New Delhi Declaration, which was issued despite scepticism about all the differences within the grouping, presented the BRICS as a formidable front in its 20th year. Among the BRICS members, the position of Saudi Arabia, which has yet to formally join the group, remains ambiguous, as Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud arrived after the main session where the joint statement was adopted on Saturday. For the other members, however, the consensus was clear on issues of global importance. The declaration made a call for the reform of the Security Council and support for a greater role for Brazil and India while recommending new initiatives for global governance. It condemned western sanctions and tariffs and resolved to improve intra-BRICS trade and transact more in local currencies. It also condemned unilateral wars, without criticising any member. While the statement omitted references to the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran, the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, and of Iran’s retaliatory attacks on its neighbours, especially the UAE, it is understood that this was due to a last-moment compromise effected between the two countries so as to forge the agreed text. It also took an exceptionally strong position on Israel’s actions in Palestine and Lebanon.
India’s fourth BRICS chairship has given ballast to its reputation as a Global South balancer with easy access to both sides of a divided world, while delivering bilateral benefits. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s close attention to Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian would have gone some way in assuaging hurt feelings, when New Delhi appeared to be tilting towards the U.S. and Israel in the war. Mr. Modi’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping also afforded the two countries a chance to reaffirm their political will to normalise ties. And his meeting with important leaders from the ASEAN grouping and African nations paid much-needed attention to India’s ties with them. This BRICS Summit will be remembered for a moment of solidarity among countries that have many differences but are together in desiring a shift in traditional power equations to one more driven by their emerging economies.

questions.question:
Consider statements (I), (II), and (III). Which are correct according to the passage?

(I) The 18th BRICS Summit presented the grouping in its 20th year.
(II) The New Delhi Declaration directly criticized specific member states responsible for unilateral wars.
(III) The position of Saudi Arabia remains ambiguous as its Foreign Minister arrived after the joint statement was adopted.
options: Only (I) and (III)
Only (II) and (III)
Only (I) and (II)
Statements (I), (II), and (III)
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Only (I) and (III)' is correct:** Statement (I) is directly supported by the passage ("presented the BRICS as a formidable front in its 20th year"), and Statement (III) is explicitly stated ("the position of Saudi Arabia... remains ambiguous, as Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud arrived after the main session where the joint statement was adopted").

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Only (I) and (II)': Incorrect because Statement (II) directly contradicts the text, which states that the declaration condemned unilateral wars "without criticising any member."
• 'Only (II) and (III)': Incorrect because Statement (II) is false according to the passage.
• 'Statements (I), (II), and (III)': Incorrect because Statement (II) contradicts the text's explicit statement that no members were criticized.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true according to the passage?
options: The New Delhi Declaration omitted direct references to the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
The New Delhi Declaration strictly prohibited all BRICS members from maintaining trade relations with Western nations.
The summit facilitated the highest-level bilateral meeting between Iran and the UAE since the West Asian war began.
Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister arrived after the main session where the joint statement was adopted.
questions.correct_answer: The New Delhi Declaration strictly prohibited all BRICS members from maintaining trade relations with Western nations.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'The New Delhi Declaration strictly prohibited all BRICS members from maintaining trade relations with Western nations.' is correct:** The passage states that the declaration "condemned western sanctions and tariffs and resolved to improve intra-BRICS trade," but it never claims that trade with Western nations was strictly prohibited, making this statement untrue.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'The New Delhi Declaration omitted direct references to the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.': This is true as the text explicitly mentions this omission was part of a last-moment compromise.
• 'Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister arrived after the main session where the joint statement was adopted.': This is true according to the second paragraph of the text.
• 'The summit facilitated the highest-level bilateral meeting between Iran and the UAE since the West Asian war began.': This is true as the passage commends the government for ensuring Iran and the UAE used the occasion for this meeting.

questions.question: What can be reasonably inferred from the passage?
options: Diplomatic compromises were required between contrasting member interests to produce an agreed joint declaration.
New Delhi appeared to tilt towards the U.S. and Israel because Prime Minister Modi paid close attention to Iran’s President.
Iran and the UAE held a bilateral meeting because the declaration condemned Israel's actions in Palestine.
Saudi Arabia delayed joining BRICS because the joint statement was adopted on a Saturday.
questions.correct_answer: Diplomatic compromises were required between contrasting member interests to produce an agreed joint declaration.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Diplomatic compromises were required between contrasting member interests to produce an agreed joint declaration.' is correct:** The passage notes that omissions regarding recent military attacks were due to a "last-moment compromise effected between the two countries so as to forge the agreed text," directly supporting this inference.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'New Delhi appeared to tilt towards the U.S. and Israel because Prime Minister Modi paid close attention to Iran’s President.': This reverses the causal relationship; Prime Minister Modi paid close attention to Iran's President to assuage hurt feelings caused by New Delhi's perceived tilt toward the U.S. and Israel.
• 'Iran and the UAE held a bilateral meeting because the declaration condemned Israel's actions in Palestine.': The passage does not establish any causal link between the bilateral meeting and the declaration's stance on Israel.
• 'Saudi Arabia delayed joining BRICS because the joint statement was adopted on a Saturday.': The arrival on Saturday was the reason its stance remained ambiguous at the session, not the cause of its delay in joining the group.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning in this context: 'ballast'
options: Stability
Sanctions
Ambiguity
Compromise
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Stability' is correct:** In the context of "given ballast to its reputation as a Global South balancer," 'ballast' means providing stability or firm support to India's diplomatic position.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Ambiguity': Incorrect because 'ambiguity' refers to uncertainty, which the passage applies to Saudi Arabia's position, not India's reputation.
• 'Compromise': Incorrect because 'compromise' refers to mutual concessions made between Iran and the UAE, not the steadying effect implied by 'ballast'.
• 'Sanctions': Incorrect because 'sanctions' refers to economic penalties condemned in the text, completely unrelated to ballast.

questions.question:
Which combination of the statements is accurate according to the passage?

(1) The Summit’s success was measured in part by intra-BRICS trade cooperation mechanisms.
(2) The declaration called for a greater role for Brazil and India in global governance.
(3) Western sanctions and tariffs were praised as beneficial for emerging economies.
(4) Narendra Modi met with Chinese President Xi Jinping to reaffirm political will to normalise ties.
options: Statements (1), (3), and (4)
Statements (1), (2), and (4)
Statements (2), (3), and (4)
Statements (1), (2), (3), and (4)
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Statements (1), (2), and (4)' is correct:** Statements (1), (2), and (4) are directly confirmed by the text. Statement (3) is false because the text explicitly states the declaration "condemned western sanctions and tariffs."

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Statements (1), (3), and (4)': Incorrect because Statement (3) is the direct opposite of what the passage states.
• 'Statements (2), (3), and (4)': Incorrect because Statement (3) contradicts the passage.
• 'Statements (1), (2), (3), and (4)': Incorrect because Statement (3) is included, which is false.

questions.question: What evidence does the author provide to support the claim that India acts as a Global South balancer?
options: Prime Minister Modi engaged in key meetings with leaders of Iran, China, ASEAN, and African nations.
Saudi Arabia successfully brought rivals Iran and the UAE together for high-level bilateral talks.
Brazil initiated last-moment compromises to omit sensitive references to the West Asian conflict.
The United States mediated discussions between India and China to normalise their bilateral ties.
questions.correct_answer: Prime Minister Modi engaged in key meetings with leaders of Iran, China, ASEAN, and African nations.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Prime Minister Modi engaged in key meetings with leaders of Iran, China, ASEAN, and African nations.' is correct:** The passage describes PM Modi's outreach to Iran's President, his meeting with Xi Jinping, and his meetings with ASEAN and African leaders as proof of India balancing its ties across a divided world.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Saudi Arabia successfully brought rivals Iran and the UAE together for high-level bilateral talks.': Incorrect because this action was attributed to the host nation (India/the Summit context), not Saudi Arabia.
• 'Brazil initiated last-moment compromises to omit sensitive references to the West Asian conflict.': Incorrect because the last-minute compromise was effected between Iran and the UAE, not Brazil.
• 'The United States mediated discussions between India and China to normalise their bilateral ties.': Incorrect because the passage states Modi met Xi Jinping directly to reaffirm their political will, without U.S. mediation.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: Unilateral Wars: The Collapse of Intra-BRICS Cooperation
Saudi Arabia: The New Leader of the BRICS Alliance
18th BRICS Summit: Forging Multilateral Consensus Amid Global Divides
The Complete Dissolution of Western Trade Hegemony
questions.correct_answer: 18th BRICS Summit: Forging Multilateral Consensus Amid Global Divides
questions.explanation:
**Why '18th BRICS Summit: Forging Multilateral Consensus Amid Global Divides' is correct:** The passage focuses primarily on how the 18th BRICS Summit achieved consensus on reformed multilateralism, trade, and joint declarations despite member differences and global wars.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Saudi Arabia: The New Leader of the BRICS Alliance': Incorrect because Saudi Arabia's role is described as ambiguous and it has not even formally joined the group.
• 'The Complete Dissolution of Western Trade Hegemony': Incorrect because it misinterprets the text's reference to condemning Western tariffs as an absolute elimination of Western dominance.
• 'Unilateral Wars: The Collapse of Intra-BRICS Cooperation': Incorrect because the passage emphasizes the success and solidarity achieved at the summit rather than a collapse of cooperation.
